title (copy, edit me): Unicorn gear: first ecommerce store
bullets (one per line, roles only):
> Right after college, I started an ecom business with my roommate. It started as dropshipping. First, we set up a Shopify store, designed a logo, and hooked up Oberlo to AliExpress for dropshipping. I had limited Photoshop skills back then and manipulated an existing logo I found on Google Images. Then we went full on private labeling, packed bags to Asia, and toured 3 factories in Shenzhen.
> We private labeled beanies with built-in Bluetooth speakers. Everything was learned from YouTube videos, blogs, and asking friends.
> A lot goes into building a brand from scratch. Beyond the operational, supply chain, and inventory management, all this was learned from content online:
- Optimizing the Shopify store
- Facebook ads
- Copywriting
- Photoshop for product lays and content
- SEO
- Google AdWords and Shopping
- Email marketing
> (No AI tools back then!)
> Not to mention the brand identity and positioning. We built target personas, reworked USPs, and asked friends for feedback.
> The result: about 60 units sold, and we only made back 50% of the cost of the initial order. Failure by a business sense.
> Looking back at this now, there was so much learned:
- We were selling a seasonal, non-evergreen product.
- Audience was small. Not everyone is cold, wears beanies, or does snow sports.
- Our initial copy and ads were too feature focused: "latest Bluetooth technology" vs. "a concert-level listening experience that feels like floating on clouds".
- Not enough validation and product feedback: friends and family were too nice and did not give honest feedback.
> Most importantly, it led me to where I am today. Growth and digital marketing is so much fun. Marketing principles are the same today. But there are loads of new tools to use, problems to solve, and stories to share.
